questions: Should the function handle elements of any type (e.g., strings, tuples, custom objects) or only numeric types as shown in the examples?
Is the sorting order always ascending, or should it follow a different rule (e.g., descending, natural order)?
If an element appears multiple times in one or both lists, does it matter for uniqueness? (The clarification mentions 'unique sorted elements', but is duplication in input irrelevant?)
Should the function preserve the original order of elements before sorting, or is sorting mandatory as stated?
What should happen if the lists contain non-hashable elements (e.g., lists, dicts) that cannot be added to a set?
Is the comparison for common elements based on value equality (==) or identity (is)?
Should the function handle nested lists or only flat lists? (e.g., common([[1,2], [3]], [[1,2]]) )
Are there any constraints on list length or performance expectations (e.g., time complexity)?
